RG Failure Rate of a Markov Chain

Source: R/04_rg.R
rgf.Rd

Compute the discrete-time RG failure rate as the logarithmic decrease in reliability over one time step.

Usage

rgf(x, time, up)

Arguments

x

An object of class MarkovChain.

time

A nonempty nonnegative integer vector of discrete time points. Values must be less than .Machine$integer.max; missing and infinite values are not allowed.

up

Integer-valued numeric vector of state positions or character vector of state names giving the operational states. Missing values are not allowed. Duplicates are ignored; empty and full state sets are valid. States are used in their order in x.

Value

A numeric vector of the same length and order as time, containing RG rates, with Inf and NaN as described above.

Details

Equation (2.9) of Sadek and Limnios (2002, p. 1842) defines $$r(t)=\log\{R(t-1)/R(t)\}, \quad t\geq1, \qquad r(0)=-\log R(0).$$ When the reliability ratio is defined, this equals \(-\log(1-\lambda(t))\), with BMP rate \(\lambda(t)\). The implementation reuses the normalized survival recursion underlying bmpf(), avoiding underflow of the raw reliability powers. It uses log1p() for small failure probabilities and the directly computed conditional survival probability when the BMP rate is close to one. The initial distribution is treated as fixed.

If \(R(t-1)>0\) but \(R(t)=0\), the rate is Inf. If both are zero, the defining ratio is undefined and NaN is returned, rather than applying the zero-rate convention of bmpf(). At time zero, \(R(0)=0\) gives Inf. Full operational sets have rate zero.

References

Sadek, A., and Limnios, N. (2002). Asymptotic properties for maximum likelihood estimators for reliability and failure rates of Markov chains. Communications in Statistics - Theory and Methods, 31(10), 1837–1861. doi:10.1081/STA-120014916 .

See also

bmpf(), rel(), vcov_rg()

Examples

P <- matrix(c(0.8, 0.2, 0.3, 0.7), nrow = 2, byrow = TRUE)
x <- MarkovChain(c(0.4, 0.6), P)
rgf(x, time = 0:3, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.9162907 0.2231436 0.2231436 0.2231436
vcov_rg(x, time = 3L, up = 1L)
#> [1] 0.4166667
